I've been farming this same land for 30 years. My father farmed before me. I know this soil, I know the weather in Quzhou, and I know what gets me through the year. My 3.5 mu isn't going to make us rich, but my son and daughter-in-law send money back from the city, so I don't have to gamble with the harvest. I want a solid, reliable yield, not an experiment.

**Wheat (winter):** I'll sow in mid-October after the summer maize is off. I always use improved seed — Jimai or Shimai varieties that the village seed shop carries. Hybrid isn't really done for wheat here, and traditional seed gives me lower yields. I put down base fertilizer at sowing — diammonium phosphate and urea mixed in — then topdress nitrogen at jointing in spring. My total nitrogen comes out around 18 kg per mu, which is what my neighbors do and what I've done for years. I do 4 irrigations: the winter watering before freeze, jointing stage, heading, and grain fill. That's standard here with the wells. I spray herbicide in spring and do one fungicide pass for powdery mildew around heading. Rotary tillage after maize harvest to break up the stubble. I expect around 450 kg per mu.

**Maize (summer):** Right after the wheat combine finishes in June, I direct-seed maize the same week — no time to waste. I always buy hybrid seed, that's just how it is, everyone does. Yields are better and I can't afford to mess around. I apply less phosphorus and potassium to maize since the soil still has residual from wheat. Nitrogen I split — base at seeding, topdress at jointing. Summer gets rain, so I only irrigate if it's dry at tasseling or grain fill — maybe twice in a bad year. One pesticide pass for corn borer, maybe one more if aphids show up bad. No tillage, just direct seeding into the wheat stubble to save fuel and time. I expect 500 kg per mu.

I won't change what works. The land is small, the family depends on it being consistent.
